meta.title: Hue, Vietnam: The Imperial City and Beyond
meta.channel: Old, Alone and Far From Home
meta.description:
During my time in Vietnam, I have experienced Da Nang and Hoi An, both cities that are considered tourist spots. Hue, which is also located along the country's Central Coast, also attracts many visitors. It has, however, a more authentic feel.

In this video, go with me through the streets of the city, checking out its charm and beauty. Of course, I visit The Imperial City. That's a UNESCO World Heritage site, which not that long ago, was home to emperors from the ruling dynasty.

Music provided by Epidemic Sound.

I am a couple of years into full-time travel. I choose destinations that are located all around the world and show what those places are like from my perspective. I subscribe to the slow travel method and I make all of these journeys by myself. Solo travel can be extremely liberating.

I invite you to see the places that I have been. That might give you ideas about where you would like to travel and possibly, areas that you want to avoid. If you are content staying at home, this channel will serve to provide you with a window onto the world. Either way, you will see some amazing sights, every time you click play!

comments.author: @sjuhav
comments.text:
I just discovered your wonderful videos today, as I'm planning to go to Vietnam again next month. Your videos are very professionally made and your voice and content, makes me wonder if you were in broadcasting in your working life. I dabble myself with photography/videography myself as a hobby.
I am also thinking your videos deserve to be presented in 4k as your videos are hands down the best travel videos I have seen. Also appreciate that you do not drown the videos in loud music.

comments.author: @oldaloneandfarfromhome
comments.text:
Thank you for such a wonderful comment. I did spend my career in the television industry, with news and production.

I shoot my video in 4K, but output in 1080. I like the freedom that gives me to manipulate the clips. I didn't think it would make that much difference for the YouTube platform.

comments.author: @sjuhav
comments.text:
⁠Thank you for taking the time to reply, and to confirm my "suspicion". I also record in 4k  and downsample to 1080p for storage reasons. But I realize that when watching the reel on a 4k 75" TV I do notice a slight difference, although my wife says she doesn't, hehe. But it is the way you tell a story with your choice of words and video scenery that is what makes your production great. 
Will follow your future adventures to get inspiration and enjoyment.
